newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto-linked groups in huge Astra deals.
newsitem.headline: Suharto-linked groups in huge Astra deals.

text.p: Business interests close to President Suharto picked up sizeable holdings in Indonesia's largest car manufacturer Astra International this week, and may be looking for a controlling stake, brokers said on Friday.
They said the Nusamba group and the Salim group could be holding shares representing up to a 30 percent stake in Astra.

Nusamba, headed by timber tycoon Muhamad "Bob" Hasan, is 80 percent owned by three charitable foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan and the president's eldest son Sigit Hardjojudanto own 10 percent each.
The Salim group is controlled by Liem Sioe Liong, believed to be Indonesia's wealthiest man and a close Suharto associate.

The stock exchange in Indonesia's second city, Surabaya, reported on Friday that some 144 million shares of Astra, about 14 percent of the company's equity, were traded on the bourse on Thursday in deals worth 603.4 billion rupiah ($262 million).
It made no mention of buyers or sellers, but brokers said the Nusamba and Salim groups were buying shares from state-owned banks and pension funds.
"It doesn't really matter, they are all the same person," said the head of one foreign brokerage. "They just want to retain control through different names."
None of the people involved were available for comment.
The broker said some 56 million shares had also been traded on the Jakarta exchange, adding this could represent the sale of a part of the stake held by tobacco magnate Putera Sampoerna.
Sampoerna, the head of cigarette company PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, bought a 9.81 percent stake in Astra last month amid reports he was attempting a takeover.
A subsidiary of PT Sampoerna then bought an additional 2.85 percent, which it has said it sold this week at a proft of some eight billion rupiah.
Brokers said Sampoerna was probably pressured to sell his stake.

"We estimate he (Sampoerna) has sold some 7.5 percent of the company," the foreign broker said. "He's lucky that he made a quite a bundle out of that and he's got away without any major political scrapes."

"These politically connected groups have got the shares they want already. They're just waiting to cross them," said the research head of another foreign brokerage. "So, small investors are getting out. Foreign investors don't like the idea of the first family controlling the company because political risk will be higher."
Brokers also dismissed comments by State Secretary Murdiono this week that the government did not want to see any one group gain control of Astra.
"They will probably stick to the letter of that," said one foreign broker. "The shares will be held by various groups all close to the family."
Japan's Toyota Motor Co owns 8.26 percent of Astra.
Astra shares closed at 3,950 rupiah on Friday, down 50, but volumes were low, brokers said.
